\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{بہت} (bahut)}{بہت (bahut)}]{\ur{بہت} (bahut) — very; a lot}

\label{lesson:UR-C375-bahut}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for reliance, then the Urdu for to insist.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{بہت}}
\textbf{\ur{بہت}} — \emph{bahut} — \textquotedblleft{}very; a lot\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اگر} \ur{بہت} \ur{سردی} \ur{ہوئی} \ur{تو} \ur{ہم} \ur{گھر} \ur{پر} \ur{رہیں} \ur{گے۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{agar bahut sardī huī to ham ghar par raheṅ ge.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If it is very cold, we will stay at home.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{بہت}} (\emph{bahut}) is inherited: CDIAL lists the Hindi cousin \emph{bahut}, \textquotedblleft{}much, many\textquotedblright{}, under Sanskrit \emph{bahutva}, \textquotedblleft{}abundance\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 9190).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bahut}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bahut}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{agar bahut sardī huī to ham ghar par raheṅ ge.} — If it is very cold, we will stay at home.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for reliance, then the Urdu for to insist, then say \emph{bahut} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{بہت} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Very; a lot\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{انتہائی} (intihāī)}{انتہائی (intihāī)}]{\ur{انتہائی} (intihāī) — extreme; extremely}

\label{lesson:UR-C375-intihai}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for to insist, then the Urdu for very.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{انتہائی}}
\textbf{\ur{انتہائی}} — \emph{intihāī} — \textquotedblleft{}extreme; extremely\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اگر} \ur{مریض} \ur{کی} \ur{حالت} \ur{انتہائی} \ur{نازک} \ur{ہے} \ur{تو} \ur{ہسپتال} \ur{جائیے۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{agar marīz kī hālat intihāī nāzuk hai to haspatāl jāiye.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If the patient is in a very bad way, go to the hospital.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{انتہائی}} (\emph{intihāī}) is built on \emph{intihā}, usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{intihāʾ}, \textquotedblleft{}the end, the furthest point\textquotedblright{}, with the ending \emph{-ī}: as far as a thing can go.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{intihāī}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{intihāī}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{agar marīz kī hālat intihāī nāzuk hai to haspatāl jāiye.} — If the patient is in a very bad way, go to the hospital.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for to insist, then the Urdu for very, then say \emph{intihāī} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{خوب} (khūb)}{خوب (khūb)}]{\ur{خوب} (khūb) — thoroughly; plenty}

\label{lesson:UR-C375-khub}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for very, then the Urdu for extremely.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{خوب}}
\textbf{\ur{خوب}} — \emph{khūb} — \textquotedblleft{}thoroughly; plenty\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اگر} \ur{تم} \ur{خوب} \ur{پڑھو} \ur{گے} \ur{تو} \ur{امتحان} \ur{پاس} \ur{کرو} \ur{گے۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{agar tum khūb paṛho ge to imtihān pās karo ge.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If you study hard, you will pass the exam.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{خوب}} (\emph{khūb}) is usually traced to Persian \emph{khūb}, \textquotedblleft{}good, fine\textquotedblright{}; Urdu uses it for doing a thing well and fully.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for very, then the Urdu for extremely, then say \emph{khūb} again

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{زبردست} (zabardast)}{زبردست (zabardast)}]{\ur{زبردست} (zabardast) — tremendous; terrific}

\label{lesson:UR-C375-zabardast}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for extremely, then the Urdu for thoroughly.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{زبردست}}
\textbf{\ur{زبردست}} — \emph{zabardast} — \textquotedblleft{}tremendous; terrific\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اگر} \ur{یہ} \ur{فلم} \ur{زبردست} \ur{ہوئی} \ur{تو} \ur{ہم} \ur{پھر} \ur{دیکھیں} \ur{گے۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{agar yih film zabardast huī to ham phir dekheṅ ge.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If this film is terrific, we will watch it again.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{زبردست}} (\emph{zabardast}) is usually traced to Persian \emph{zabardast}, \textquotedblleft{}having the upper hand\textquotedblright{}: \emph{zabar}, \textquotedblleft{}above\textquotedblright{}, and \emph{dast}, \textquotedblleft{}a hand\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for extremely, then the Urdu for thoroughly, then say \emph{zabardast} again
\end{itemize}
